success_patterns: Track the full quantifier scope and parameter dependence in each option: preserve exact endpoints and index ranges, and distinguish every case from sufficiently large cases or constants that may depend on an additional parameter.
Keep the theorem's hypotheses attached to its conclusion. Do not extend a result from a specified subclass to all objects, or replace generic and almost-everywhere claims with universal ones.

Audit each added strengthening separately. Existence and uniqueness are distinct; exactly one and at most one agree only when existence is independently guaranteed. Global existence also does not by itself imply estimates uniform over all time.

For piecewise classifications and exact formulas, compare every branch condition and expression, including boundary cases, indices, signs, and coefficients; a close paraphrase is not a substitute for the complete claim.

patch.reasoning: The existing skill already emphasizes exact comparison and strength, but these successes reinforce a few practical checks for near-matching choices. Making nested quantifier scope, implicit existence, time-uniform bounds, and branch-by-branch formula comparison explicit may help avoid unsupported strengthenings—the recurring failure pattern noted in the previous step.

edits.content:
## Near-variant audits
- Read uniformity claims with their full quantifier nesting: distinguish, for example, a constant chosen after an auxiliary parameter from one independent of it, and a result for every parameter value from one only for sufficiently large values. Preserve exact endpoints and index ranges.
- Check each added clause independently. Global existence does not imply estimates uniform over all time; estimates on each finite horizon may have constants depending on that horizon. Likewise, an at-most-one conclusion is equivalent to exactly one only when existence is already guaranteed.
- For piecewise classifications, compare every case condition and its associated expression. Verify endpoint inclusion, exceptional cases, and that an otherwise clause covers precisely the remaining cases; do not accept a prose summary or near-matching formula in place of the exact classification.
